title: One series, three sums
sub: Partial sums of 1 − 1/2 + 1/3 − 1/4 + …, added in different orders.

frames.caption: The alternating harmonic series 1 − 1/2 + 1/3 − 1/4 + …, in its usual order. Its partial sums zigzag in toward ln 2 ≈ 0.693.
400 terms: partial sum 0.6919. It converges, but only conditionally: the positive terms alone (1 + 1/3 + 1/5 + …) diverge, and so do the negative ones.
Exactly the same terms, reordered: take positive terms until the sum passes 1.5, then negative terms until it drops below, and repeat. Every term is used once, eventually.
10 terms: partial sum 1.2718. So far: 8 positive terms and 2 negative ones, in an order chosen to aim at 1.5.
400 terms: partial sum 1.5001. Same numbers, different order, different sum: 1.5. Because both halves diverge, there is always enough of either to steer anywhere (Riemann's rearrangement theorem).
Exactly the same terms, reordered: take positive terms until the sum passes −0.5, then negative terms until it drops below, and repeat. Every term is used once, eventually.
10 terms: partial sum -0.4145. So far: 1 positive terms and 9 negative ones, in an order chosen to aim at -0.5.
400 terms: partial sum -0.4957. Same numbers, different order, different sum: −0.5. Because both halves diverge, there is always enough of either to steer anywhere (Riemann's rearrangement theorem).
